newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares at new high on Telekom ruling.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares at new high on Telekom ruling.

text.p: High-flying Turkish shares on Thursday soared to their 15th record close this year in record volume, after a court ruling paved the way for the privatisation of Turk Telekom, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 index closed at an all-time high of 1,352, up 101 points, or 8.07 percent from Wednesday's previous high of 1,251.
The market index has surged 38.5 percent since end-1996.
Daily volume hit a record of 43.46 trillion lira ($377.3 million), up from Wednesday's 29.40 trillion ($255.2 million) and a previous high of 35.89 trillion lira ($311.5 million) last November.

The constitutional court rejected a challenge by 116 opposition MPs to the Telekom sell-off and only cancelled a clause regarding the legal supervision of GSM mobile phone service licence agreements by the Council of State.
The government expects to raise $3.5 billion from Telekom privatisation and another $1 billion from GSM licence agreements later this year.
Brokers said the market's upward movement was expected to continue.
"The rally will continue tomorrow but investors must be aware that some share prices have already risen too much," said Turgay Ozaner from Global Securities.
Ozaner said the index would reach the "1,500 level soon."
Of the 237 shares traded today, 211 advanced, only 10 declined and 16 closed stable.
The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN rose 7.01 percent to 1,405, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ gained 5.83 percent to 1,306 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL surged 9.42 percent to 1,336.
Largely state-owned firms were among the most active shares.

Flat steel maker Eregli was up 2,250 lira at 19,750 and Turkish Airlines rose 3,500 lira to 33,500. Among utilities Aktas Elektrik rose 17,500 lira to 155,000 and Cukurova Elektrik jumped 12,500 lira to 162,500.
